clue.text: Disengaged response, with dislike greatly reduced

parts.note: to hate is to dislike strongly

indicators.note: reduced tells us the word for greatly loses its final letter

parts.note: very means greatly

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a matter, their strong aversion having faded to indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts VERY to VER. The answer runs across two lights, 1 and 27 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'whatever' is the classic bored, uninterested reply that signals the speaker has stopped caring.

clue.text: American prankster's obscure initiation of ritual

parts.note: to haze something is to obscure it, as mist does

indicators.note: the initiation, or start, of the word ritual supplies its opening letter

explanation.surface: An American practical joker with a murky induction ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: In US colleges hazing is the bullying of newcomers, often as an initiation ritual, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a hazer is someone who subjects newcomers to humiliating tricks or pranks.

clue.text: Finished half of this part of the golf course

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word this is its first two letters

parts.note: the rough is the long grass beside the fairway on a golf course

explanation.surface: A golfer has done half of this stretch of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: To be through with something is to have completed it, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Hoping for a different outcome that's attractive

definitions.meaning: ... a court ruling is asking a higher court for a different result

explanation.surface: A wish that things turn out otherwise is a charming one.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is lodging a legal appeal against a verdict; the other is being pleasing or charming.

clue.text: Girl losing head, the fool

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for girl drops its first letter

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman who loses her head is a silly fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a stupid person, a common insult for someone foolish.

clue.text: Prepare anaesthetic for five?

definitions.note: five is an example of the answer, hence the question mark

parts.note: to prime something is to prepare it for use
an anaesthetic is something that makes you number, that is more numb

explanation.surface: Getting a painkiller ready for patient number five.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as 'more numb', not as a count; the question mark flags that five is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Five is divisible only by one and itself, so it is an instance of this kind of integer.

clue.text: Mean to show anger after five taken into A&E

indicators.note: after places the anger word following the hospital part
taken into describes the numeral being admitted inside the hospital letters

parts.note: A&E is the accident and emergency department, giving its two letters
V is the Roman numeral for five
rage is anger

explanation.surface: Someone tries to show fury after five people are admitted to casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of figures is its average, a mathematical synonym.

clue.text: Come between priest and one undergoing conversion

indicators.note: conversion means changing form, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A third party intervenes between a cleric and a would-be convert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergoing conversion' rearranges PRIEST and ONE; the religious surface makes conversion look spiritual.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to place oneself between two parties, a direct synonym for intervening.

clue.text: End lack of interest, ditching one new way of resolving ties

parts.note: a goal is an end one aims at

indicators.note: ditching tells us these letters are thrown out of the longer word

parts.note: indifference is a lack of interest
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Ending apathy by getting rid of one new way to settle draws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching' removes I and N from INDIFFERENCE. In football leagues teams level on points are separated by goals scored minus goals conceded.
explanation.definitionFit: When teams finish level on points, the tie is usually broken by comparing goals scored and conceded.

clue.text: Holiday attraction, unlikely tool adopted by anti-racists?

indicators.note: adopted by places the shuffled tool inside the movement's name

parts.note: Black Power was a movement against racial oppression

indicators.note: unlikely suggests the word tool is twisted into an improbable arrangement

explanation.surface: A resort attraction that campaigners against racism took up as an improbable instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' hides the anagram inside the movement's name. The answer is a Victorian tower at Blackpool, a seaside resort in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Lancashire seaside landmark is a major tourist draw for people on holiday.

clue.text: Revived figure idly cut a plan that's incomplete

indicators.note: cut means the word for idly is chopped, here in half

parts.note: lazily means idly

indicators.note: incomplete tells us the scheme word loses its last letter

parts.note: a ruse is a scheme or plan

explanation.surface: A dozy sketch of a plan left unfinished, with a risen figure in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' halves LAZILY to LAZ; 'that's incomplete' trims RUSE to RUS.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel of John, Jesus raises Lazarus from the dead, the archetypal person brought back to life.

clue.text: Ship heading off — then a return to island? It shows reluctance to move

indicators.note: heading off means the ship word loses its first letter

parts.note: a liner is a passenger ship

indicators.note: return to says the island word is read backwards

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A ship sets off, then heads back to an island, but something resists going anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return to' reverses AIT to TIA; 'heading off' drops L from LINER. 'then a' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the physical property of resisting a change in motion, and figuratively a reluctance to act.

clue.text: Collection of writings left in church cell

parts.note: a corpus is a body or collection of written works

indicators.note: in places the left letter inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A set of manuscripts abandoned in a monk's room at church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cell' looks like a monk's room in the surface, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpuscle is a blood cell, so it is one kind of cell in the body.

clue.text: Telegram slipped under yellow mesh

indicators.note: in a down answer, slipped under puts the telegram word below the cowardly word

parts.note: yellow and chicken both mean cowardly
a wire is an old word for a telegram

explanation.surface: A telegram pushed beneath a yellow mesh screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken wire is a light wire netting with a hexagonal mesh, used for poultry runs.

clue.text: Help to secure credit coming with a sting

indicators.note: to secure suggests holding the credit abbreviation inside the help word

parts.note: aid is help
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Assistance in arranging a loan that comes with painful strings attached.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid smell or taste is sharp and bitter, one that stings the nose or throat.

clue.text: Cryptic cultured Phi — something very attractive

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or obscure, signalling these two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: The setter Phi, being mysterious and refined, praises himself as gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi is this puzzle's setter, so the surface is self-flattery; 'Cryptic' rearranges CULTURED and PHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulchritude is a formal word for physical beauty, the quality of being very attractive.

clue.text: Source of poisoning? Induce discomfort with half of it

parts.note: to lead someone to do something is to induce them
pain is discomfort

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word it is taken as its second letter

explanation.surface: Something toxic? It causes unease, with half of it hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: old house paint was a common cause of poisoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint containing lead compounds was widely used until its toxicity, especially to children, became known.

clue.text: Inappropriate entry of oboe: very loud

indicators.note: the entry of a word is its first letter, where one comes in

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: An oboe comes in at the wrong moment, blaring very loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entry' plays on a musician's entry in a score.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark that is off is unsuitable or out of order, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Eggs are very old when rejected

indicators.note: rejected, meaning sent back, reads these letters in reverse

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Some eggs are thrown out because they are very old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when rejected' turns AVO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the plural of ovum, the egg cell of a female animal.

clue.text: Contradict sources of vigorous explanation provided by brand — it's pretence

indicators.note: provided by puts the brand word ahead of the rest

parts.note: a make is a brand of product
to belie something is to contradict it

indicators.note: sources of takes the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A firm's forceful account turns out to be contradicted: all a sham.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-believe is pretending or fantasy, the playful imagining of something untrue.

clue.text: Two-thirds of armies busy acquiring metal rifle

indicators.note: acquiring means the jumbled letters take the metal inside them
busy suggests bustling movement, so those four letters are jumbled
two-thirds of the six-letter word armies is its first four letters

parts.note: tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Most of the troops, kept busy, are acquiring metal guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' turns ARMI into MARI, which then takes in TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Martini-Henry was a breech-loading rifle used by the British Army in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Amount of greenery in meadow beginning to fall over long time

indicators.note: in a down answer, over puts the meadow and fall parts above the long time

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of fall

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: How much foliage in a meadow is starting to drop over a long period.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage means foliage, the leaves of plants collectively, so it is the green growth present.

clue.text: Light, light touch provided with hesitation

parts.note: a tap is a light touch
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A gentle tap given with a moment's hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'light' tempts us to read both as adjectives; the first is a noun, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a thin candle or wick used to light lamps and candles, so a source of light.

clue.text: Something telling son to nick a costly car

indicators.note: to nick means to steal or take, so the native word takes the car and a inside it

parts.note: a native son is someone born in a place, so native stands for son
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, a famously expensive car

explanation.surface: Something tells a boy to steal an expensive car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something telling' is a story that tells, not something revealing; a 'native son' is a man born in a place, which licenses son for the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is a story or account, literally a piece of telling.

clue.text: Foolish way the game and league will end?

wordplay.reading: GAME and LEAGUE each finishing with the letter E

parts.words: way the game and league will end?
parts.note: the clue asks how the two words game and league finish, which is the same final letter for both

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a match and a championship will finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting surface hides a spelling joke: both words end in E, giving IN AN E.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or pointless, a synonym for foolish.

clue.text: Endless delay — equipment twice running short in Hawaiian location

indicators.note: endless means the delay word loses its last letter

parts.note: to wait is to delay

indicators.note: twice says the shortened kit word appears two times
running short means the equipment word lacks its final letter

parts.note: kit is equipment

explanation.surface: An unending wait while gear twice runs out at a Hawaiian spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Waikiki is a beach district of Honolulu on the island of Oahu, Hawaii.

clue.text: A sheep I included in account in Biblical language

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: included in puts the letter I inside the account abbreviation

explanation.surface: A shepherd's ledger in the tongue of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic, a Semitic tongue, was spoken by Jesus and appears in parts of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Some muscles not present? Not half

indicators.note: not half means only half of the absent word is kept, its opening three letters

parts.note: absent means not present

explanation.surface: A query about missing muscles, answered with a British 'not half!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very much'; here it keeps only the first half of ABSENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abs is informal for abdominal muscles, a group of muscles in the stomach.

clue.text: Testy behaviour resistant to change

indicators.note: to change means the letters of resistant are rearranged

explanation.surface: Irritability that refuses to alter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resistant to change' reads as one phrase, but 'to change' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattiness is British slang for irritability, being ratty or bad-tempered.
